```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The coach is for people practising, not for training a model. It works
offline, without a language model, and says nothing the rules engine or a
search has not established. Every statement carries its claim type:

| Claim type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `legal_fact` | follows from the rules alone (a capture, a check, a promotion) |
| `searched` | found by a bounded search; the budget, depth and completeness are given |
| `heuristic` | an assessment by a stated definition (a fork, a hanging piece) |
| `learning_suggestion` | advice for practice, not a claim about the position |

"Forces checkmate" appears only when every reply has been checked.

## Explaining an action

Squares are always named with their board, so overlapping coordinates are
never confused.

```{r}
st <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game()$state
ex <- gambitR3D::g3_explain_action(st, "m:W:0:0-N:1:0")
ex
```

German text is available for every template:

```{r}
gambitR3D::g3_explain_action(st, "m:W:0:0-N:1:0", lang = "de")$text
```

## Reviewing a game

The review compares each played action with the best analysed alternative
under the same evaluator and budget, replays every line it shows through the
engine, and marks the critical decisions.

```{r}
game <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game()
for (i in 1:16) {
  if (gambitR3D::g3_is_terminal(game$state)) break
  agent <- if (game$state$side == "white") "random" else "search"
  d <- gambitR3D::g3_choose_action(game$state, agent, budget = list(nodes = 3000L), seed = i)
  game <- gambitR3D::g3_game_apply(game, d$action_id)
}
review <- gambitR3D::g3_coach_game(game, budget = list(nodes = 3000L))
review
```

## Exercises from the game

Exercises come from real analysed positions. An exercise is "validated" only
when its criterion has been checked against every legal action under the saved
rules hash; several answers may be accepted. An exercise that rests on a
bounded search stays a candidate.

```{r}
exs <- gambitR3D::g3_create_exercises(review, max_n = 5L)
exs$summary[, c("theme", "status", "n_legal", "n_solved", "n_acceptable")]
if (length(exs$exercises)) cat(gambitR3D::g3_exercise_objective(exs$exercises[[1]]), "\n")
```

The package also ships a small catalogue of authored, engine-verified
exercises:

```{r}
cat_ex <- gambitR3D::g3_exercise_catalogue()
cat_ex$summary[, c("theme", "status", "n_solved")]
```

## Hints and attempts

Hints come in four levels: the area or threat, the piece or platform, the
destination, and finally the full action with a verified continuation. A level
never reveals what a later level would.

```{r}
ex1 <- cat_ex$exercises[[1]]
cat(gambitR3D::g3_exercise_objective(ex1), "\n")
for (level in 1:2) cat(level, ":", gambitR3D::g3_exercise_hint(ex1, level)$text, "\n")
legal <- gambitR3D::g3_legal_actions(ex1$start_state)$action_id
attempt <- gambitR3D::g3_score_attempt(ex1, legal[1], hints_used = 2L)
attempt$status
cat(attempt$feedback, "\n")
```

An illegal input gets its own feedback, separate from a legal but weak move.

## The learner profile

Progress is kept in a local JSON file that you choose. It stores attempts, hint
use and themes, and plans practice with a transparent spaced schedule: missed
themes come back, mastered ones are mixed in, and every selection says why it
was chosen. It makes no claims about ratings or personal traits.

```{r}
profile <- file.path(tempdir(), "learner.json")
gambitR3D::g3_learner_record(profile, attempt)
plan <- gambitR3D::g3_practice_plan(profile, cat_ex, daily_limit = 3L)
plan[, c("theme", "reason")]
gambitR3D::g3_learner_settings(profile)
```

Using games for practice and including them in a training dataset are separate
settings; the second is off unless you switch it on. Nothing is uploaded: there
is no upload function. `g3_learner_export()`, `g3_learner_delete()` and
`g3_learner_reset()` (the last two need `confirm = TRUE`) give you control over
the file.
